title: Marvelous Designer Magazine Vol. 4: A Global Celebration of Creativity

![fb6be3dec43645b7a7b769ebba7dc5fb](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/10f2fe0f75dc4a21a368a764975993c7/images/fb6be3dec43645b7a7b769ebba7dc5fbMagazine_1.png)

We are thrilled to introduce the latest edition of Marvelous Designer Magazine, celebrating the artistry of our worldwide user base. Vol. 4 brings together 26 exceptional works from 28 talented artists, offering an intimate look at the talent driving our community forward.

  
Beyond the stunning visuals, this issue provides a wealth of knowledge through expert interviews and detailed technical workflows. We are especially excited to highlight the artistry of **Ngan Hoang** in this edition, whose work is deservedly featured on the cover.

  
We invite you to explore the creative process and get inspired by the cutting-edge techniques shared by our featured pros. As we celebrate these achievements, we are already looking for the next wave of fresh talent. Continue creating, sharing, and innovating—**you could be featured in our next volume!**

title: Dunes of Steel | 3D Cinematic Animation
content:
## _3D artist_[ _Konstantin Batishchev_](https://www.behance.net/gallery/246698533/Dunes-of-Steel-Cinematic-Environment-Design) _takes us to a desolate desert planet where massive industrial structures rise from the dunes, driven by mysterious underground mechanisms. Discover how he pushed his technical workflow to the limit to transform a raw concept into a polished, high-fidelity cinematic masterpiece._

* * *

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z7TP8F4HwX4?start=0

# **Software Used**

Cinema 4D – Modeling, animation  
Cascadeur - Character animation  
Marvelous Designer – Cloth Simulation   
Substance Painter – Texturing  
Octane Render – Lighting & Rendering  
Embergen - smoke simulation  
After Effects - Post-Production

#   
**Artist Introduction**

Hi, I’m a Motion Designer with over 10 years of experience working in 2D and 3D animation. I focus mostly on creating visuals for branding, product videos, and storytelling. In my work, I usually handle the whole process - from the initial idea and look development to animation, simulations, rendering, and final compositing.

I especially enjoy working on cinematics and character animation, so in both personal and commercial projects I focus on building a story and finding the best way to visualize it.

I work with tools like Cinema 4D, Unreal Engine, Marvelous Designer, After Effects, Blender, and Substance Painter, depending on the needs of the project.

# **Please introduce your project.**

_Dunes of Steel_ is my personal project, where I challenged myself to create a large environment, a desert atmosphere, and a sci-fi story about a character trying to sneak into the center of a city — a huge burning crater.

![d8a9055ec9c8479d8c1486013ab74c01](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/d8a9055ec9c8479d8c1486013ab74c01City_Shot1_00111.png)The city design and its materials, especially the pipes, show that this is an industrial city that depends on the crater.

I really enjoyed working on the details and textures. It was important for me to show the scale of the environment and how sand and heat affect the materials.

I started by choosing a music track, which I used as a base for the animation and editing. The rhythm of the track shaped the whole pacing of the video.

The project took me about a month from idea to final render, which surprised me — usually my personal projects take much longer.

There is also a lot of compositing in this project. Elements like smoke were simulated and rendered in Embergen, then composited in After Effects.

![7453b8d9dddc440cb6e6087994ccc8f7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/7453b8d9dddc440cb6e6087994ccc8f7Dunes%20of%20Steel.png)

# **Tell us how Marvelous Designer creates value in this project.**

For _Dunes of Steel_ , cloth simulation plays a key role - it’s a visual focus on the character that adds complexity and creates a strong contrast against the metallic environment.

![9fbba222bd0e49d498897f66e1c97915](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/9fbba222bd0e49d498897f66e1c97915Process.gif)  
In fact, improving my cloth simulation skills was one of the main reasons I started this project. Most of the scenes were created in Marvelous Designer, except for the final shot where the cloak is dropped - that simulation was done in Cinema 4D, since I needed more precise and flexible control over the cloth movement.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=94cpPzT7vWI?start=0

  
In most of the cloth simulations, there were no issues because the movements were smooth and natural.

![65708e6e70054843a941dc2f55b6be42](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/65708e6e70054843a941dc2f55b6be42jump-1.jpg)![0caf358ce99b412495127eadeb8305d5](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/0caf358ce99b412495127eadeb8305d5Run.gif)  
The difficulties started in the landing scene. In this case, I needed to art direct the cloth simulation so that it wouldn’t just look realistic, but also look visually appealing.

In the first example, I only use Time Warp, but the wind is too weak, so I’m not satisfied with the result.

![624b6735be63462083d69d4db81c66b4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/624b6735be63462083d69d4db81c66b4time-1.jpg)  
In the next example, I increase the wind strength, but I don’t start the simulation from the very beginning. This is a very convenient workflow. The cloth movement during the character’s flight already looks good to me, so I continue the simulation starting from the landing moment. The result is better, but I still don’t like how the cloth behaves. 

![7304cbc6e2e14a0a92d26a36f118e605](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/7304cbc6e2e14a0a92d26a36f118e605time-2.jpg)  
Then I increase **air damping**. Because of that, when the character moves in slow motion, the cloth also behaves like it’s in slow motion. But it still doesn’t fall to the ground properly because the wind and air resistance are stronger. 

![72673e3fd12641a0809e19c127948eb8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/72673e3fd12641a0809e19c127948eb8air-1.jpg)  
In the final version, I increase gravity, and the cloth finally moves the way I want. This way, I was able to control the simulation, and it looks very realistic at normal speed. 

![ec47e4f73fb843829354f7f69ae157cf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/ec47e4f73fb843829354f7f69ae157cfLanding_4.gif)

# **What is your favorite feature or tool to use in Marvelous Designer?**

I don’t have extensive experience with Marvelous Designer yet, so I’m probably not using it to its full potential. 

What I like most is that making clothes feels just like in real life - you don’t have to fake seams, and you can tweak any part in real time to fit the character perfectly. I know it’s a pretty basic feature, but I really enjoy it 🙂

# ![be4e9e4310d947e8991ee6f60005fab2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/be4e9e4310d947e8991ee6f60005fab21_Final.png)![5b1e46ffd3fa4e01a9f4c6516c47640e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/5b1e46ffd3fa4e01a9f4c6516c47640e2_Final.png)![12ea29a348394edfb460a886b3b3a722](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/6a24e7e458a448948d97f6bc8b998165/images/12ea29a348394edfb460a886b3b3a722cape%20render.png)  
**For other users considering Marvelous Designer for a cinematic project, do you have any advice or experience to share?**

In my project, when simulating cloth, I used Time Warp. This is a key parameter that helps make the simulation more accurate. Animated characters often have fast movements, which can cause incorrect simulations because the distance between frames is too large, and the cloth can intersect with the object.

I also recommend experimenting with wind direction, wind strength, and gravity. These settings can really help you guide the cloth and get the motion you want.

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T-6BsPwfWWQ?start=0
content_description: Explore how 3D artist Konstantin Batishchev expertly combines advanced cloth simulation and cinematic environment design to bring the desolate industrial world of *Dunes of Steel* to vivid life.

title: Trouble registering accessories in MD
content:
Hello. I'm using MD and I'm having a problem registering the shoes I have designed as accessories. They look fine until I register them, and then they come out with the heel part all twisted up. I don't know how to fix this so any help will be greatly appreciated. Thanks.![9748b308c72b449c979c33e833497813](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202605/075c6dd382a24cbcaf5ca8e431dc1a3e/images/9748b308c72b449c979c33e833497813shoes%20error-horz-vert.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: This problem is quite common. You can try the following steps: after adjusting the model's heel upwards, export the model. Then, in an external software, fit the shoes properly. Add a transparent object to fill the gap between the heel and the sole, which can interfere with the binding. Next, export the shoes to CLO. Use the virtual model with the heel upward to add the shoes, and this should solve the problem.
Reply 1: Thank you. Let me try this.
content_description: A support page for users experiencing issues with registering and correctly displaying custom-designed shoe accessories in MD.

title: Shimmer - Escena Animation Studio
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/363d6e56f6e64a678245ae4558d4a686Selected%20April%2029%202026%201443.jpeg)_From Student Dreams to Ariel Awards: How Escena Animation Studio Crafted the Soul of ‘SHIMMER’_

# **Studio Introduction**

Hello! I'm Alan Narvaez, the CFX Supervisor at Escena Animation Studio, the in-house studio of Escena, a school for animation and digital art based in Mexico City. EAS focuses on non-commercial projects that provide our students with their first opportunity to work in a collaborative environment and pipeline.

Although we are a small studio, each of our members is full of artistic talent, and we consider ourselves more of a family than a workplace. We are currently working on six different projects, which we are eager to share more soon and we’re very happy to be here sharing our experience with you. 

# **Congratulations on winning the Best Animated Short award at the Ariel Awards, presented by the Mexican Academy of Cinematographic Arts and Sciences (AMACC)! Could you tell us more about your project, ‘SHIMMER’?**

Thank you so much! Sure, Shimmer is a film about a man far too obsessed with his work to be a good dad and a daughter too proud to admit she’s out of her depth when it comes to striking out on her own. It’s about two characters with too much hubris and too little grace for one another entrenched in a struggle that will tear them apart. It’s about repentance and understanding that come too late to fix what’s been steadily eroded by neglect.

![4cae3b135e8f44618ec91a9e7aca59b1](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/4cae3b135e8f44618ec91a9e7aca59b1Image01.png)![20159cb4d8654e15bcfee49c86707b94](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/20159cb4d8654e15bcfee49c86707b94Image02.png)![57242c65e4c348ebb179d78b681002d3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/57242c65e4c348ebb179d78b681002d3Image03.png)

# **Why did you decide to use Marvelous Designer? How did it help you serve art direction?**

We decided to use Marvelous because its tools, such as layer clone over, morph target and attach to measure, helped us to accelerate and work more efficiently when interpreting conceptual art in 3D. We used Marvelous not only for character clothing, but also as a simulation engine for all character shots. One of the many advantages of using Marvelous's physics engine was its use of layers; I don't know of any other program that works with layers in simulation. In the CFX department, Marvelous was our closest ally and most loyal friend.

One particularly challenging aspect was the hammock simulation. We experimented with numerous presets until we found the right one, adjusting the damping value and reducing the particle distance significantly to achieve the desired movement.

![e50220c7fe244447b701ce0b923ca371](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/e50220c7fe244447b701ce0b923ca371ezgif-20bf5a33c470f897.gif)First, we tried to bring the hammock model from Maya to Marvelous only for simulation, but that did not go well. Then we decided to make it from scratch in Marvelous, only exporting the posts that were going to serve as supports, then we brought the alembic with the animation of the posts and also “Matias” who was going to be our passive collider.

We needed to make the hammock follow the animation of the posts, so we used a lot of tacks on avatar to prevent them from coming loose. We also used a lot of strength on the small supports of the hammock so we wouldn't have to deal with separations.

![9259737620c54932a51d017cf199063a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/9259737620c54932a51d017cf199063aezgif-362df06322eb4771.gif)

For the shot where the cart collapses the hammock, we had to create a proxy because there was too much geometry interacting with the fabric. So we simplified the model, making it easier to control. But first, we had to simulate the helmet on its own to ensure it had the correct silhouette and didn't appear to be floating.

![d3193b49cb814724bb8f7ec79e50675b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/d3193b49cb814724bb8f7ec79e50675bezgif-2b46c9f42e1fe977.gif)

# **Which part of the garment did you focus on the most to perfectly achieve the desired silhouette?**

I think the most difficult garment was “Mati’s” jumper. We wanted to make the knot as realistic as possible, but also avoid any problems during the simulation stage, so we faked it with line tacks, which helped us achieve the final look. 

![9e7e1577a8bf47019c25a4bc275b0dd4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/9e7e1577a8bf47019c25a4bc275b0dd4Image04.png)![910cd7a43e834c85b9c0cee4b7ee79ea](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/910cd7a43e834c85b9c0cee4b7ee79eaImage05.png)![232240fa000d41e5b6b9e8ed2a6a68cc](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/232240fa000d41e5b6b9e8ed2a6a68ccezgif-2e23862fc60ed4d3.gif)With Ricardo, most of the problems occurred during the simulation. We had a lot of movement shots, so to prevent the coat from disappearing, we increased the scene time wrap each time. This was really helpful.

We wanted the inside of his coat to be padded. To achieve this, we used a layer clone. 

![91289e6e10594b448a92fc00fe288058](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/91289e6e10594b448a92fc00fe288058Image06.png)![0a58ad8a71b84b25bf9b67bda6e34749](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/0a58ad8a71b84b25bf9b67bda6e34749Image07.png)

The challenge with Lucia was her jeans, which had to fit perfectly inside her boots. We used the 'Attach to Measure' tool around the final edge so that, once the simulation department had finished, the jeans wouldn't come off no matter how much movement there was.

![9d75cabfe3a9432cb365e05471278f3f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/9d75cabfe3a9432cb365e05471278f3fImage08.png)![07d2914b44d040e0a59c1642e754e769](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/07d2914b44d040e0a59c1642e754e769Image09.png)

# **Could you share some of your personal 'optimization know-how' for translating 2D concept art into 3D?**

As tailoring artists, we often need to find numerous real-life references to clothing. Concept art alone is not enough, since there are properties of fabric that cannot be fully conveyed in drawings. We often use our own clothes to understand how certain seams or patterns work, which helps us to achieve a result that is as close as possible to the concept art.

Once we have researched enough references, we can start creating the patterns. Since we were also going to simulate in Marvelous, these had to be in good proportion to the model, so we paid close attention to the strain map. 

![2e29f98123d24abbb491b4eb1735e6e3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/2e29f98123d24abbb491b4eb1735e6e3Image10.png)Once we had achieved the desired silhouette and proportions with a fairly relaxed strain map, we exported the asset and sent it to the textures department. They were responsible for giving the clothing a dirty and aged look.

Upon arriving at the simulation department, we imported the animation from Maya and positioned the clothing in the initial pose of the shot. We achieved this using Marvelous' morph target, after which we could start the simulation process.

![ada3d7b06d4e4b3d8b944afbe843ad24](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/ada3d7b06d4e4b3d8b944afbe843ad24Image11.png)![adfbe34fb4854a3a86bccbdf75b984f0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/adfbe34fb4854a3a86bccbdf75b984f0Image12.png)![92b2369a9f60409da1b82d9f71718408](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/92b2369a9f60409da1b82d9f71718408Image13.png)  
![66fb475bec0c43258b8f2053dbcc603a](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/66fb475bec0c43258b8f2053dbcc603aezgif-37ab277a7d5ab861.gif)

# **Many students and aspiring designers are inspired by your work. Do you have any advice for creators who are just starting with Marvelous Designer or dreaming of winning international awards like you?**

Never give up! I know that sounds clichéd, but it's genuinely the best thing you can do. Like everyone else, I started out as a student, and through hard work, I managed to secure a position at the studio. I later worked on Shimmer as a teacher and have seen students give up because of the pressure. However, those who truly strive always surprise me by achieving things that many professionals never reach. Working with students and observing their professional development and progress is always very rewarding.

What they're working on doesn't matter, as long as they give their best effort and dedication. They should focus on enjoying the process, not the result.

# **As technology evolves, the role of digital garments is becoming even more significant. How do you plan to push the boundaries with Marvelous Designer in your future projects, and what’s next for your studio?**

One thing I love about Marvelous Designer is that they're constantly releasing new versions with lots of new tools, which encourage me to keep developing as an artist. It's exciting to experiment with all the new tools available.

As I mentioned earlier, we're working on six new projects, which I can't reveal much about, but I can say that one of them features lots of beasts and demons. I'm really enjoying dressing up characters with those characteristics.

![2fad1a044e0b4295b517fa78121def41](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/2fad1a044e0b4295b517fa78121def41Image15.png)![66dbfa3f7f7f4f50b4acb0489f4af7b7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/66dbfa3f7f7f4f50b4acb0489f4af7b7Image16.png)![e9460d81a1404dd6bff75daff968fdd8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202604/bcfad0156fb7462ea9c2afcc4f74a252/images/e9460d81a1404dd6bff75daff968fdd8Image17.png)
content_description: Showcasing Escena Animation Studio’s award-winning journey and expert use of Marvelous Designer to bring authentic digital garments to life in the animated short ‘SHIMMER,’ inspiring aspiring creators through behind-the-scenes insights and future project previews.

Our core mission is to break down language barriers so you can focus 100% on your creative work. Instead of digging through long manuals, simply ask the chatbot for a much faster and smoother onboarding experience!
